verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.title: Canine Thorax · Lateral + Annotated VHS Example
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.credit: Original radiograph: Ophélie TISSIER; annotated version by Uwe Gille · CC BY-SA 4.0 · https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/

images.caption: Unannotated lateral thoracic image; side of recumbency and normality not established by source.
Derivative of this canine thoracic radiograph with vertebral heart score markings.

verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.history: Source image shows a large dog in lateral recumbency; patient complaint and final diagnosis not provided.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.quality: Check thoracic field coverage, respiratory phase, sternum/spine overlap, exposure, and positioning.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.findings: Identify cardiac silhouette and vertebral bodies. The annotated derivative demonstrates a vertebral heart score measurement concept; it is not a validated clinical conclusion about this patient.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.interpretation: Anatomy and VHS technique reference. A vertebral heart score should be interpreted with breed, age, projection and clinical context.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.differentials: Not assigned; source does not establish a disease.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.why: The VHS method expresses long- and short-axis heart silhouette dimensions relative to thoracic vertebral length; interpretation depends on species/breed and acquisition.
verified-canine-thorax-lateral-vhs.next: Practice identifying measurement axes on the original view, then check the annotated derivative. Correlate a measured score with patient context.

verified-canine-thorax-vd.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-thorax-vd.title: Canine Thorax · Ventrodorsal Reference

images.caption: Ventro-dorsal projection from a large dog; do not assume the same animal as the lateral example.

verified-canine-thorax-vd.history: Large dog; clinical history not specified.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.quality: Assess centering, thoracic symmetry/rotation, lung coverage, laterality and exposure indicator if available.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.findings: Practice identifying right and left lung fields, cardiac silhouette, diaphragm, ribs and mediastinum.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.interpretation: Projection recognition reference; radiographic normality is not independently confirmed.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.differentials: No source-confirmed diagnosis; avoid inventing one.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.why: VD beam travel is ventral to dorsal. Rotation distorts the appearance of bilateral thoracic structures.
verified-canine-thorax-vd.next: Use alongside a true patient-matched lateral view whenever making clinical interpretations.

verified-feline-thorax-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.title: Feline Thorax · Age-Related Bronchial Wall Mineralization
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.credit: AurelioAHeckert · Public domain dedication (Commons file description)

images.caption: The source report describes normal-sized cardiac silhouette and mineralized bronchial walls; view side not established.

verified-feline-thorax-lateral.history: Female domestic cat; report in source describes age-related bronchial wall calcification, without additional clinical history.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.quality: Confirm entire thorax included, correct projection/markers and adequate inspiration.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.findings: Source interpretation: heart silhouette within normal parameters; bronchial wall calcification described as a senile change; no radiographic findings suggestive of pulmonary metastasis in the views studied.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.interpretation: Source-reported bronchial wall calcification; no radiographic metastatic pattern reported. This is not equivalent to excluding all lung disease.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.differentials: Bronchial mineralization may be age-related; assess for concurrent inflammatory airway patterns with clinical correlation.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.why: Mineralized bronchial walls can create conspicuous ring/tram-line opacities; recognize chronic or age-related changes without automatically diagnosing active bronchitis.
verified-feline-thorax-lateral.next: Correlate with respiratory history, prior imaging and orthogonal views.

verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.title: Feline Abdomen · Normal GI Appearance + T13–L1 Spondylosis

images.caption: Source describes GI tract as apparently normal and T13–L1 spondylosis.

verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.history: Source: 12-year-old overweight (BCS 6/9) castrated male cat imaged for suspected swallowed bone.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.quality: Check abdominal coverage and positioning; single-view examinations have limitations.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.findings: The source describes gastrointestinal appearance as unremarkable but notes spondylosis between T13 and L1.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.interpretation: No obvious GI finding described in this source image; T13–L1 spondylosis is a distinct radiographic finding.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.differentials: Clinical gastrointestinal obstruction may still warrant further evaluation; spondylosis may be incidental.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.why: Spondylosis involves degenerative osseous bridging/osteophytes, which may be unrelated to the presenting digestive complaint.
verified-feline-abdomen-right-lateral.next: Correlate with examination and additional imaging if clinical concern persists.

verified-canine-gdv-lateral.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.title: Canine GDV · Lateral Abdominal Radiograph

images.caption: Source-identified side-view X-ray of gastric dilatation–volvulus (GDV).

verified-canine-gdv-lateral.history: The source identifies a canine GDV radiograph but supplies no complete clinical signalment.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.quality: Check that the distended stomach and relevant abdomen are included; side of lateral projection is not provided.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.findings: Assess gastric distension and abnormal intragastric gas compartmentalization suggestive of volvulus. Identify the gas/fluid pattern from the actual view.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.interpretation: Source-labeled example of canine gastric dilatation–volvulus.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.differentials: Simple gastric distension and alternative gastric outflow problems; interpret with clinical status.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.why: Gastric torsion can occlude venous outflow and compromise perfusion; time-critical shock and tissue injury can develop.
verified-canine-gdv-lateral.next: Emergency stabilization and immediate veterinary surgical assessment; do not delay lifesaving care for additional views.

verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.reviewStatus: Source-derived educational interpretation; not independent specialist reading
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.title: Equine Laminitis · Annotated P3 Rotation
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.credit: Malcolm Morley (radiograph), Froggerlaura (annotations) · public domain (Commons file description)

images.caption: P2 and P3 labeled; yellow/white distance lines demonstrate change in dorsal hoof-wall-to-P3 relationship.

verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.history: Source describes a laminitic horse foot, without full individual history.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.quality: Original annotation is part of the image. Later unannotated views may be added to the same case.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.findings: The source identifies an increased distance between the distal portion of P3 and the dorsal hoof wall, indicating displacement/rotation in the laminitic example.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.interpretation: Annotated source-identified laminitis with distal phalanx rotation relative to the hoof wall.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.differentials: Other causes of hoof pain or altered phalangeal alignment require clinical and radiographic correlation.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.why: Damage to the lamellar suspension of P3 can allow its position within the hoof capsule to change.
verified-equine-laminitis-annotated.next: Interpret with lameness findings and standardized farriery/radiographic measurements; assess urgent support and treatment.
